stem: Which document sets out the duties and responsibilities of a job?

options.rationale: Correct: it describes the job.
This describes the person needed, not the duties.
A CV is written by the applicant.
A reference is a view from a previous employer.

explanation: A **job description** gives the job title, duties, responsibilities and conditions.

options.content: Filling a vacancy with an existing employee
options.rationale: Correct: the person already works for the business.

options.content: Advertising a vacancy in a national newspaper
options.rationale: That is external recruitment.

options.content: Using an employment agency to find staff
options.rationale: Agencies find people outside the business.

options.content: Training new staff when they join
options.rationale: That is induction training.

explanation: **Internal recruitment** fills a vacancy from within the business, often by promotion.

stem: Which item would appear on a person specification?

options.content: Deliver goods to customers throughout Masvingo province each week
options.rationale: That is a duty: job description.

options.content: At least two years' experience of driving heavy vehicles
options.rationale: Correct: experience required of the person.
Reporting lines are in the job description.
Hours are working conditions: job description.

explanation: A **person specification** lists qualifications, experience, skills and personal qualities.

stem: Which is an advantage of external recruitment?

options.content: It is cheaper than recruiting internally
options.rationale: External recruitment usually costs more.

options.content: The candidate already knows the business and its staff
options.rationale: That is true of internal recruitment.
New external staff need induction.

options.content: It brings new ideas and skills into the business
options.rationale: Correct: outsiders have different experience.

explanation: External recruitment widens choice and brings fresh ideas, but costs more and takes longer.

stem: A bank wants to check how honest and reliable an applicant was in her previous job. Which selection method is most useful?

options.rationale: A test shows skill, not honesty.
She writes the CV herself.

options.content: The advertisement she replied to for the job
options.rationale: An advert attracts applicants; it is not a selection method.

options.content: A reference from her previous employer
options.rationale: Correct: the employer can comment on honesty and reliability.

explanation: **References** give an independent view of an applicant's character and reliability.

stem: Why might a business use an employment agency rather than advertising a vacancy itself?

options.content: Agencies are always cheaper than advertising
options.rationale: Agencies charge fees, which can be high.

options.content: Agencies guarantee that the new employee will stay in the job for many years
options.rationale: No agency can guarantee that.

options.content: The agency finds and shortlists suitable candidates, saving managers' time
options.rationale: Correct: agencies do much of the recruitment work.

options.content: It allows the business to recruit internally
options.rationale: Agencies find external candidates.

explanation: Agencies save time and have lists of candidates, but charge a fee.
hints: What work does the agency do for the business?

stem: A furniture factory wants to know whether applicants can actually operate a wood-cutting machine. Which selection method is best?

options.rationale: Forms show what applicants claim, not ability.
Correct: it shows actual ability on the machine.
That shows personality, not machine skill.
Talking about the skill does not prove it.

explanation: A **skills test** shows real ability; interviews and forms only show claims.
hints: Which method shows what a person can do, not what they say?

stem: Selection is the process of choosing the best applicant from those who have applied.
explanation: True. Recruitment attracts applicants; selection chooses between them.

stem: Internal recruitment creates no further vacancy in the business.
explanation: False. The employee who is promoted leaves a job that must also be filled.

stem: Match each selection method with what it shows best.

right.content: Actual ability to do a task
Standard information that is easy to compare
A previous employer's view of reliability

explanation: Each selection method gives different evidence, so businesses often use several.

stem: Put the stages in order by completing the sentence.

payload.template: After writing the job description and person specification, the business {{blank:a}} the vacancy, {{blank:b}} the best applicants and then interviews them.

explanation: Advertise → shortlist → interview and test → appoint.

stem: Name the document written by a job applicant that summarises his or her education, experience and skills.
explanation: A **curriculum vitae (CV)** is the applicant's own summary.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why a business writes a person specification before advertising a job.

points.description: Shows the qualifications / skills / experience needed.
So the advert attracts suitable applicants / unsuitable people do not apply.
Provides criteria to compare applicants.
So shortlisting is fair and quicker / best person selected.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The person specification sets out the qualifications and experience needed, so the advert can state them and unsuitable people do not apply. It also gives managers a fair checklist for comparing applicants when shortlisting.

explanation: It guides the advert and makes shortlisting fair.
hints: Think about the advert and the shortlist.

stem: A supermarket chain needs a new branch manager for its Kwekwe store. Discuss whether it should recruit internally or externally.

points.description: Internal: knows the chain's systems; cheaper and quicker.
Internal: promotion motivates other staff; ability already known.
Internal: creates another vacancy; no new ideas.
External: new ideas and experience from other retailers; wider choice.
External: costly, slower, needs induction; existing staff may be demotivated.
Justified conclusion, e.g. internal if a capable deputy exists.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Internal recruitment would be cheaper and quicker, and a deputy from another branch already knows the chain's systems and has proved his or her ability; promotion also shows other staff they can progress. However, it leaves another vacancy and brings no new ideas. External recruitment gives a wider choice and new experience from other retailers, but is more expensive, slower and needs induction, and staff who hoped for promotion may be demotivated. If the chain has a capable deputy manager, it should recruit internally; if the Kwekwe store needs a turnaround, an experienced outsider may be better.

explanation: Weigh cost, speed, motivation and knowledge against new ideas and choice.
hints: Does the chain already have deputy managers who could be promoted?

stem:
Mazowe Agro-Dealers sells seed, fertiliser and tools to farmers. It needs a branch manager for its new shop in Chinhoyi. The person specification says a diploma in agriculture is essential and experience of managing staff is essential. Three applicants were shortlisted.

| Applicant | Diploma in agriculture | Managed staff before | Source | Interview score (out of 10) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Tendai | Yes | Yes | Internal (deputy) | 6 |
| Rudo | Yes | Yes | External | 9 |
| Sipho | No | Yes | External | 8 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which applicant should be removed because he does not meet an essential criterion?

options.rationale: She meets both essential criteria.
He meets both essential criteria.
Correct: he has no diploma in agriculture.
One applicant lacks the essential diploma.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Identify **three** methods Mazowe Agro-Dealers could use, other than an interview, to select the branch manager.

points.description: References.
Tests (e.g. numeracy, stock-control skills).
Application form / CV / assessment day.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend whether Tendai or Rudo should be appointed. Justify your answer.

points.description: Tendai: internal, knows products, systems and farmers; cheaper and quicker.
Tendai: promotion motivates staff; but lower interview score (6).
Rudo: highest interview score (9); may bring new ideas.
Rudo: external, needs induction; existing staff may feel overlooked.
Both meet essential criteria, so other factors decide (e.g. references, tests).
Justified recommendation.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Both Tendai and Rudo meet the essential criteria. Tendai is the deputy, so he knows the products, the stock system and many farmers; appointing him is quicker and cheaper and shows other staff that promotion is possible. However, his interview score was only 6. Rudo scored 9, suggesting stronger communication and ideas, but she would need induction and staff may feel overlooked. A new shop needs someone who can start immediately and knows the business, so I recommend Tendai, provided his references are good, with training in the areas where his interview was weak.

explanation: Remove applicants who fail essential criteria, then weigh interview performance against internal knowledge.
hints: (c) Use every column of the table.

stem: Thandeka owns a growing travel agency in Harare and needs three booking clerks. In the past she advertised on a notice board outside the office and chose people she liked at a short chat. Two of her last four clerks left within three months, and one made costly booking errors.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **two** contents of a job description for a booking clerk.

points.description: Job title / to whom the clerk reports.
Duties (e.g. making bookings, issuing tickets) / hours and conditions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** weaknesses in Thandeka's present recruitment and selection methods.

points.description: Notice board reaches few people.
So little choice of applicants / suitable people may not see it.
Short chat with no tests or references.
So she cannot judge skill / reliability, leading to errors and staff leaving.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A notice board outside the office reaches very few people, so she has little choice of applicants. Choosing people she likes after a short chat does not test booking skills or check references, which explains the costly errors and clerks who left quickly.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend how Thandeka should recruit and select the three clerks. Justify your answer.

points.description: Write a job description and person specification first.
Advertise online / social media / local newspaper to reach more applicants cheaply.
Shortlist against the person specification.
Use a test of booking / computer skills and check references.
Structured interview with the same questions for all.
Justified recommendation with cost / benefit weighed.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Thandeka should first write a job description and person specification, so she knows what skills she needs. She should advertise online and on social media, which is cheap and reaches many young people with computer skills. She should shortlist against the specification, then give a practical booking test and ask every candidate the same interview questions, and check references. This takes more time and some cost, but it is cheaper than the errors and replacements caused by her present methods.

explanation: A structured process (documents, wide advertising, tests and references) reduces costly mistakes and labour turnover.
hints: (b) Think about who sees the advert and how she chooses.
